note: Compact product catalog for the Coworker's audience-building task. Seeded from src/lib/productCatalogExtras.ts (anonymized copy, industry-shape numbers). target_signals are the reasons a product is relevant now and are the only thing that can create a match. qualifying_signals corroborate a match and raise its score but can never create one, so a trait like paying a card in full cannot by itself pitch a travel card. disqualifiers are hard exclusions the institution applies and must suppress a household regardless of fit. As of v2, card products carry machine-readable `terms` so annual benefit is computed from the household's own transactions against the published rate card rather than a flat heuristic. `incumbents` holds the terms of what a household already carries, so benefit can be stated net of what they earn today. Every product also carries `plain_benefit`: what it does differently, in client-safe words with no figures. Taglines quote rates, and a rate in a client draft fails validateClientDraft, so the tagline cannot be the thing an outreach draft is built from. As of v4, the thirteen original products carry the signal vocabulary from the 55-product bank catalog. As of v5, the other forty-two products from that catalog are here too, each with its target/qualifier/block lists as the bank wrote them and the eleven universal blocks applied. Most of the tokens here are not emitted by anything today and are inert by design: they describe the target state and cost nothing until detection catches up. Four tokens are carried in both spellings — "Cash-advance / gambling spend" alongside "gambling spend", and "Volatile income" alongside "income_instability" — because the pipeline emits the long form and dropping it would quietly switch off a working block or, for overdraft protection, its only working target. Three qualifiers the bank already knows from the relationship record — monthly_surplus, owns_home, high_net_worth, multi_product_household — are derived from the household file rather than authored as signals, and already_holds_product is enforced against products_held. Priced terms: cards compute from the household ledger, deposits from idle cash against the baseline rate, refinances from the named balance and rate fields; everything else states what the product is for.

spend_categories.note: Maps an earn category to the transaction subcategories that count toward it. Used by the benefit calculator so category math is data-driven, not regex guesswork.

card_ineligible.note: Debits that are not card purchases and therefore earn nothing on any card. Excluded from every side of the benefit calculation, including the current-earn baseline.

incumbents.note: Rate cards for cards a household already holds with us, so benefit can be stated net of what they earn today. A household whose card we do not hold gets no entry here on purpose: their current earn is unknown rather than zero, and the calculator reports gross with that gap stated instead of inventing a baseline.
